title: Continuous torus pullback is integrable
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb R^n$, let $p\in[0,\infty]$, and let $F$ be a continuous real-valued function on the torus $(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}}$. Define a map from $\mathbb R^n$ to this torus by sending $x$ to the point whose coordinate indexed by $(i,0)$ is $x_i$ modulo $1$ and whose coordinate indexed by $(i,1)$ is $\sqrt2 x_i$ modulo $1$. Then the composition of $F$ with this map belongs to $L^p(\mu)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ is a finite measure on $\mathbb R^n$
$F$ is continuous and real-valued on the specified finite-dimensional torus
